riley_support: Hi @customer_mark — saw your ticket about GitHub SSO failing during the redirect step. You mentioned the app shows "Authorization failed (invalid_state)". Can you paste the browser URL you were redirected to (sanitized)?
customer_mark: sure, here's what the browser shows after GitHub redirects back (replaced tokens with Xs):
GET https://app.medtrack.io/oauth/github/callback?code=abcd1234&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9+Uw==
customer_mark: we get the error modal immediately after that. This started yesterday for a subset of users.
riley_support: thanks. @kevin_backend can you check server logs for callback handler for medtrack org?
kevin_backend: looking now. I pulled a few raw request lines from nginx access logs — incoming querystring shows state param but the value has spaces instead of plus signs: 
```
GET /oauth/github/callback?code=abcd1234&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9 Uw== HTTP/1.1
Host: app.medtrack.io
```
kevin_backend: our app expects the state to be the same base64 string we set in the cookie, but the request we see has the '+' replaced with a space which breaks the validation.
kevin_backend: tracing back through the stack, requests go through our edge nginx -> internal proxy -> auth-service. The edge nginx does a decode of the querystring for logging and later components use urllib.parse.parse_qs which treats '+' as space (application/x-www-form-urlencoded semantics). If the original redirect encodes '+' as %2B, but some component decodes it too early turning %2B -> +, then a second decode converts + to space.
customer_mark: is this an app bug or something on your infra? Some users can log in, others can't.
riley_support: looks infra-related. @tara_infra any recent changes to the edge proxies or logging middleware?
tara_infra: we did deploy a new log-processor at the edge yesterday to normalize querystrings for analytics. It has a component that does URL-decode for nicer logs, but it accidentally writes back the decoded URL into the forwarded request header for a subset of hosts. That's a bad bug. rolling back that change to stop mutating the forwarded URL.
deploy-bot: rollback edge-log-normalizer v3 -> v2 initiated by tara_infra at 2025-11-05T09:10:05Z
kevin_backend: after rollback I'm seeing callbacks with the original encoded state (%2B present). Re-running the flow locally with a test account: before rollback, server computed state (cookie) = eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9+Uw==, incoming request had eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9 Uw==, validation failed. After rollback incoming request preserves %2B and parse_qs yields the correct string.
customer_mark: tested now and login succeeded. great.
kevin_backend: root cause = edge log normalizer mutated forwarded URL by inserting decoded querystring (turning %2B into +) which then got interpreted as form-encoded and + became space during parsing. This broke state and PKCE exchanges for providers that use characters like + in state/code_challenge.
jenna_security: tagging this for security review; mutated URLs could potentially affect other auth flows. We'll run a quick audit of deploys with URL-decoding in the pipeline.
riley_support: action items: 1) tara to remove mutation and add a hard rule that forwarded URLs are never written back after decode. 2) kevin to change our OAuth state to use base64url (replace +/ with -_) to be resilient to '+' to space issues and add validation fallback that fixes common decodes. 3) infra to add an integration test hitting /oauth/* endpoints that verifies callback params round-trip through edge unchanged.
kevin_backend: I'll open PR to switch to base64url encoding for state & PKCE and add a lenient parser that rejects spaces but logs them for alerting. Also adding a metric oauth.callback.malformed_state_count.
tara_infra: I'll push a config patch to disallow mutating forwarded URLs and add unit tests for the log-normalizer that assert it never writes back decoded querystrings.
deploy-bot: edge-log-normalizer v2 rolled back successfully at 2025-11-05T09:12:30Z
riley_support: closing loop with medtrack; marking ticket as resolved pending postmortem. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
customer_mark: thanks team — appreciate the fast fix. Will re-open if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:
